title_tag: Best Shooting Ranges in Budapest (2026): 9 Packages Compared
meta_description: Budapest shooting ranges compared: guns, rounds, price per shot (€1.47 to €4.09), AK-47 packages, outdoor range with hotel pickup and stag group tips.
h1_main: Best Shooting Ranges in Budapest in 2026
author_role: 9 shooting packages compared on guns, rounds, price per shot, location and rules
lead: The headline price tells you almost nothing at a Budapest shooting range. Packages from €74 to €225 give you anywhere from 40 to 60 rounds, which works out between €1.47 and €4.09 a shot, and only some of them put an AK-47 in your hands.

For most first-timers the answer is Capital Shooting Range's 6-gun package: €86 for 40 rounds including an AK-47 and an M4-style carbine, an instructor for every shooter, in District VII. If you would rather shoot outdoors with the transfer sorted, Ranger's outdoor range picks you up in the centre from €85. If you want the most trigger time for your money, the newer Shooting2 packages near St Stephen's Basilica give 60 rounds over 10 guns for €90.

Below are all 9 packages across four Budapest ranges, compared on guns, rounds, price per shot, indoor vs outdoor, transfers and the rules (18+, ID, strictly sober). Filter by budget, variety or hotel pickup, and if you are planning a stag do, skip to the group section.

review: Capital is the safest default for a first shooting session in Budapest. For €86.28 you get six guns that cover the whole range of what people come for: a .22 pistol to learn the basics, two 9 mm and .45 handguns, the Stribog submachine gun, an M4-style carbine and the AK-47. That is 40 rounds, or €2.16 a shot, and the package lists an instructor for every shooter.

Compared with its neighbours it sits in the middle on price per round. The three Shooting2 packages near St Stephen's Basilica give you more trigger time for the money (44–60 rounds), while Churchill's Basic package costs about the same but gives you only four guns and no AK-47. What Capital adds is structure: briefing, lane time and a photo stop are timed, and range fees and ammunition are spelled out as included, so there are no surprises at the till.

It suits couples, solo travellers and small groups who want a straightforward, well-reviewed session in the city centre between sightseeing stops. The catch is the round count: 5 shots on the AK-47 goes quickly. Extra guns and extra rounds can be added at the venue for a fee, so decide your budget before you start.

review: Ranger is the pick when you want the shooting to feel like an outing rather than a quick stop. You are collected from central pick-up points, driven about 20 minutes to an outdoor range, and get a 2-hour guided lesson with eye and ear protection, vests and targets. The price starts at €85, the same as the city-centre ranges, but the way you buy is different: you choose between a single gun and up to 10 firearms, and extra guns and ammunition are charged on top. It also means you cannot work out a price per shot in advance the way you can with the Shooting2 or Capital packages.

It suits stag groups and friends who want a few hours out of the city and the transport handled. It does not suit a tight sightseeing day: count on 2 to 3.5 hours door to door. If you want the same operator without the drive, its indoor range in District X runs the same 2-hour lesson (#9).

review: Churchill's Basic package is the one with the deepest track record: rated 4.9 across more than 400 reviews. For €84.60 (down from €94) you fire 45 rounds through 4 guns at an indoor range on Holló utca in District VII.

The guns are modern and easy to learn on: 20 rounds on a CZ 512 Tactical, then an AR-9, a CZ Scorpion EVO and five rounds on an AR-15. At €1.88 a shot it is fair value, but it is four guns against Capital's six and Shooting2's eight to ten at a similar price, and there is no AK-47.

Choose it if accessibility matters (it is the only range here listed as wheelchair-accessible), if you want French alongside English, or if you simply trust a big pile of consistent reviews over a newer listing. The session runs about an hour, so it slots between lunch and an evening out. Arrive sober: the operator is explicit about it.

What you are buying is access to Soviet-bloc firearms you will not find in the other packages: the WWII PPSh-41 submachine gun, the DP-28 light machine gun, the Czechoslovak VZ Scorpion 61, an AK-47, the short AKSU and a Saiga-12 shotgun.

It pairs naturally with Budapest's communist-era sights (see our communist tour comparison). Expect a session of about an hour at Churchill's indoor range on Holló utca. The rating is perfect but rests on only a few reviews; the range itself is well proven through the Basic and Hollywood packages.

Reading the table: the three Shooting2 packages are the best value per round and per gun (about €9 a gun). They are newer listings with only a handful of reviews so far. Capital costs a little more per shot but includes an instructor for every shooter and has 200+ reviews behind it. • First time, want the classic mix: Capital. AK-47, M4-style carbine, pistols and a submachine gun, one instructor per shooter, €86.

  • WWII and Cold War guns: Churchill Soviet for the PPSh-41 and DP-28, or Shooting2 10-gun for the Colt 1911 and Tokarev at a third of the price.

guide.h2: Shooting on a Stag or Hen Do in Budapest
guide.html:
A range session is a strong stag or hen afternoon, and it works best before the drinking starts. Every range here bans alcohol and intoxication outright, and Churchill states that all visitors must be sober. Turn up after a long lunch with beers and you can be turned away.

Group pricing: all packages are priced per shooter. A group of 8 on the Shooting2 shotgun package pays 8 × €73.65 = €589; on Capital it is 8 × €86.28 = €690. Mixed groups work well at Ranger, where each person can choose between one gun and up to 10 at the range.

Group size: Shooting2 caps each session at 6 participants, so a group of 10 needs two back-to-back slots or a different range. Capital and Churchill do not state a cap, and Capital explicitly caters to stag parties, birthdays and team events. Ranger's outdoor package includes the bus for the whole group, which removes the taxi logistics.

How to book: put everyone on one booking so you land in the same slot, make sure every shooter brings a passport or ID card (Capital, Shooting2 and Ranger require it; Ranger accepts a copy), and check that nobody in the group is under 18. Free cancellation up to 24 hours before applies to all nine packages, so you can lock in a slot early.

Make it a day: shoot in the afternoon, then hand over to the evening. Our pub crawl comparison covers Budapest's ruin bar routes, and the Széchenyi Sparty guide covers Budapest's Saturday-night bath party. More ideas for a group weekend are in the best things to do in Budapest.

guide.h2: Rules, Getting There and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
Who can shoot: 18+ only at every range, no licence or experience required. Every package that lists restrictions excludes pregnant women. Churchill adds limits: no people with heart problems, and a minimum weight of 40 kg on the Hollywood and Soviet packages (plus 140 cm minimum height on Soviet), with upper age limits of 75–80.

What to bring: a passport or ID card (the Capital, Shooting2 and Ranger packages say so explicitly), and your phone: photos are welcome at Capital and Shooting2 when your instructor says so. Ranger supplies eye and ear protection, a protective vest and targets.

Getting there: three of the ranges are walkable from central hotels. Shooting2 is on Podmaniczky Frigyes tér near St Stephen's Basilica and Arany János utca metro (entrance between the café and the burger restaurant); Capital is at Dob utca 89 and Churchill at Holló utca 6, both in District VII. Ranger Indoor is at Maglódi út 47 in District X. Only Ranger Outdoor includes a transfer, from central pick-up points about 20 minutes from the range.

Timing: Churchill sessions take about an hour, Capital and Shooting2 about 1.5 hours including registration and coffee (arrive 15 minutes early), and Ranger runs 2-hour lessons, or 2–3.5 hours with the outdoor transfer. Indoor ranges are weather-proof, which makes them a good rainy-day plan.

What costs extra: extra guns and extra rounds at every range. Capital and Shooting2 sell add-ons on site, and Ranger prices extra guns and ammunition on top of its €85 entry package. Decide your limit before you start.

faqs.q: How much does a shooting range cost in Budapest?
faqs.a: Packages run from €73.65 to €225 per person. Most first-timer packages cost €81–90 for 40–60 rounds, which is about €1.50–2.20 per shot. The Soviet-gun package at €225 is the outlier.

faqs.q: Can I shoot an AK-47 in Budapest?
faqs.a: Yes. The Capital 6-gun package and all three Shooting2 packages include 5 rounds on an AK-47 for €74–90. Churchill's Soviet package gives 7 AK-47 rounds plus 7 on the short AKSU for €225. Churchill's Hollywood package includes 5 AK-47 rounds in one of its two advertised line-ups; the Basic package has none.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence or experience to shoot in Budapest?
faqs.a: No. Every package here is designed for beginners, with a safety briefing and an instructor or range master supervising. You must be 18 or over, and Capital, Shooting2 and Ranger ask every shooter to bring a passport or ID card.

faqs.q: Can I drink before going to a shooting range in Budapest?
faqs.a: No. All ranges ban alcohol and intoxication, and Churchill states that all visitors must be sober. On a stag do, shoot first and drink after.

faqs.q: Is there a shooting range in Budapest with hotel pickup?
faqs.a: Yes: Ranger's outdoor package includes an air-conditioned bus from central pick-up points to the range about 20 minutes away and back, from €85.

faqs.q: Which Budapest shooting range is best for a stag party?
faqs.a: For a big group, Capital (stag parties catered for, no stated cap) or Ranger Outdoor (bus included, everyone picks their own gun count). Shooting2 offers the best value but caps sessions at 6, so larger groups need two slots. Pair it with a pub crawl in the evening.

faqs.q: How long does a shooting experience take?
faqs.a: About 1 hour at Churchill, 1.5 hours at Capital and Shooting2 including registration, 2 hours at Ranger Indoor, and 2–3.5 hours for Ranger Outdoor including the transfer.

methodology: We compared 9 shooting packages at four Budapest ranges (Capital, Shooting2, Churchill and Ranger) side by side on the numbers that decide the booking: guns, rounds, price per shot and per gun, which models you fire, indoor vs outdoor, location and transfers, group size, and the age, ID and alcohol rules. Prices are live from-prices per person for a standard date in November 2026.
